chapter: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
title: Stranded in Chicago when William Poe ran off with the pay
summary: After playing a Chicago theatre the meat man William Poe vanished with the money; Bubbles hauled coal to feed the group, and Sugar Babe's mother ended the trio.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: When we got to Chicago, a fellow that we used to work for, they had us there, called William Poe, P-O-E. William Poe and he was a meat man, he handled meat and he took us to Chicago from Indianapolis and when we got to Chicago that's when we played the O'Clean Theater and he ran off with the money and we are all stranded there and the fella that was our tutor putting us on the stage in Louisville, he had his wife along with him and he was taking care of us. His name was Billy Maxey. He was a comedian, Billy Maxey was. That's the

fella, the manager of the theater in Louisville, had to dress us all, we first went on as urchins in the theater and I was just with his sister before she died. She was in Chicago and he went to New York and I saw him in New York since I've been grown and I met his sister and I only learned about her when he passed, 'cause she got in touch with me to let me know he passed and so forth and I found out when I got in touch with her she moved to Chicago from New York and in Chicago I went to see her. I got pictures of her I think and a postcard of her and I got it down to put it in my book, my story, you know. I got some data on her for my story. She liked to travel all the time. She was a warden for the women's prison in Chicago. She's got a daughter that's still in Chicago, I think.
We were stranded in Chicago with the Ink Spots doing the act at the Olean Theater — I forgot the name of the show or the people we was working with. The guy for who

we did the show and finished that engagement there and were expecting to get paid off, the man run away with the money, left us all in Chicago stranded. That's Billy Maxey, his wife, Buck, Sugar Babe and myself and at that time the weather was cold, too, and you know how the coal men drive by and put a pile of coal in front of your door, or in front of your gate, you know, on the sidewalk and the people have to get somebody to put it in. So I hauled coal into people's houses to get money enough to buy food for us and I took what little money that there was and bought us some potatas and made us a stew and everything, for Buck and I, and we had a good meal with little or nothing. And I give Maxey some money to buy food for him and his wife.
And then when we got back to Indianapolis Sugar Babe's mother wouldn't let him go any farther with us because of that incident. So we lost the three Ink Spots.
